traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and technical requirements from docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md are implemented and verified:
- Core Functionality & Requirements: The `traceability/require-branch-annotation` rule is implemented to detect missing @story and/or @req annotations on significant code branches (if/else, try/catch, switch cases, and all major loop types), using DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES and comment-gathering logic (REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION, REQ-SIGNIFICANCE-CRITERIA, REQ-COMMENT-ASSOCIATION, REQ-ANNOTATION-PARSING). Autofix behavior inserts placeholder annotations with appropriate indentation. - Quality Standards & Integration: The rule follows ESLint RuleModule structure with meta, schema, and message definitions, and is integrated into the plugin’s dynamic rule registry and recommended/strict configs in src/index.ts. Helper functions and tests show careful handling of SwitchCase, CatchClause, and else-if (formatter-aware) scenarios, covering nested branches and complex patterns (REQ-NESTED-HANDLING). - User Experience & Error Handling: Error messages clearly indicate which annotation is missing via the `missingAnnotation` message with data {missing: '@story'|'@req'}, and invalid configuration errors explicitly list allowed branch types. Tests assert both the diagnostics structure and configuration error text, and the implementation includes safe fallbacks (try/catch in comment scanning, multiple strategies for catch/else-if comment association). - Configuration & Invalid Config Behavior: validateBranchTypes implements REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE, supports custom branchTypes arrays, and returns a Program listener that reports invalid types with a clear message. Unit and rule tests cover valid custom configuration, ignored unlisted types, enforced listed types, and invalid branchTypes options. - Performance: A dedicated performance test exercises the rule on large, deeply nested branch structures and enforces a generous time budget (<5 seconds), directly satisfying REQ-PERFORMANCE-OPTIMIZATION. - Documentation: docs/rules/require-branch-annotation.md provides rule description, behavior details (including Prettier-aware catch and else-if handling), configuration options, examples of correct/incorrect code, and invalid configuration examples, matching the story’s documentation acceptance criterion. The rule is also referenced from README.md.
Given the implemented rule, helper utilities, comprehensive tests (behavioral, configuration, and performance), successful Jest run, and existing rule documentation, this story is fully implemented and validated.
